$comment: The core claim-type registry. Prose, reasoning and the rules for resolving a default live in CLAIM-TYPES.md beside this file; this is the machine-readable half an agent ships and a client reads.

maskStyles.$comment: Two edge cases are stated because two clients implementing this table independently both hit them and both had to guess. They guessed alike, which is luck rather than a specification: a value SHORTER than the tail a style keeps is masked in full, and a mask is drawn at a FIXED width rather than one character per hidden character.
maskStyles.none: Shown in full. The value is not one a shoulder can steal.
maskStyles.last2: Final two characters shown; everything before them replaced — unless the value is no longer than two, which is masked in full. `last2` of a two-character value is the value.
maskStyles.last4: Final four characters shown; everything before them replaced — unless the value is no longer than four, which is masked in full. A four-digit card number printed whole is not a masked card number.
maskStyles.emailLocal: First character of the local part, then the domain in full — a@example.com. The domain is what makes an address recognisable to its owner; the local part is what makes it usable to anyone else. A value with no local part, or no `@`, is masked in full rather than guessed at.
maskStyles.$widthComment: A mask is drawn at a fixed width, NOT one character per character hidden. A run that tracks the length publishes the length — of a passport number, a date of birth, a card — which is information the mask was drawn to withhold, and is often enough to identify the format. The exact width is the client's; that it does not vary with the value is not.

defaults.$comment: What a token resolves to when neither an exact entry nor a registered prefix supplies an axis. Deliberately the conservative answer: a vocabulary this registry has never seen is exactly the one nothing has reasoned about, and an unknown value rendered in the clear is a decision nobody made. `x:` tokens are unregistered by construction and land here too — they were two identical entries until it was pointed out that nothing said which applied.

types.$comment: A FAMILY entry, matched as a prefix. Without it `payment.somethingNew` resolves to the unregistered default, whose `release` is `consent` — weaker than every registered member of the family. A gated family must not be leavable by inventing a token.
A family entry, for the reason given on `payment`.

An exact token, not only a family prefix: a pool that keeps one undifferentiated name is using `name`, and without an entry it would mask it in full. As a prefix it makes an unknown `name.*` no *looser* than the default — a family entry can only tighten.
A former name is not a lesser name. It is the one a holder most often keeps in order to answer a question once and never show again, and the one whose casual display does the most harm.
Almost always askable as a predicate instead — see the proof rungs. A verifier wanting `over18` and receiving a birth date has taken a lifelong identifier to answer a boolean.
High because a mobile number is both a strong join key and an authentication factor at a great many services. Its harm is not embarrassment; it is account takeover.
Separate from the full address on purpose: country alone answers most jurisdiction questions and identifies almost nobody.

strictness.$comment: Ordering per axis, most protective first. A fallback takes the most protective of what a registered prefix says and what `defaults.unregistered` says — see CLAIM-TYPES.md §4. An EXACT entry is used as written and is not compared against anything.
